mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes ML 230 or 350 petrol engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt M111 engine for the ML 230 costs £2,000-£2,800 supply-only; a rebuilt M112 V6 engine for the ML 350 costs £2,400-£3,200 supply-only. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 depending on complexity - both engines are relatively straightforward to work on.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of harmonic balancer failure on a Mercedes ML 350?

acceptedAnswer.text: Engine vibration, belt noise, or visible rubber separation on the harmonic balancer are the classic warning signs on the M112 V6. The bonded rubber layer between the inner and outer sections can separate with age, causing the outer ring to slip and potentially damage accessory belts.

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes ML 230 or 350 petrol engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the M111 inline-four and the M112 V6 are among Mercedes' most straightforward and reliable petrol engines. With regular maintenance and proactive attention to known issues like timing chain wear and harmonic balancer separation, these engines routinely exceed 150,000 miles.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes ML 230 and 350 petrol engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Properly maintained M111 and M112 engines routinely reach 150,000-200,000 miles before major work is needed. These simple, robust petrol engines are known for their longevity when serviced regularly.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in my Mercedes ML 230 or 350 petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if the M Class is otherwise in good condition with no rust or major transmission faults. A rebuilt M111 costs £2,000-£2,800 - comparable to the value of a £2,000-£8,000 vehicle, making it a justifiable investment for well-maintained examples. For the ML 350, the higher value range (£3,000-£8,000) makes replacement even more viable.

mainEntity.name: What oil does my Mercedes ML 230 or 350 petrol need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes-Benz specifies MB 229.5 high-performance oil - typically 5W-30 or 5W-40 fully synthetic. The M111 requires approximately 5.5 litres; the M112 V6 requires approximately 6.5 litres.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 230/350 Petrol - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The ML 230 launched with the W163 generation in 1997 as the entry-level petrol M Class, powered by the M111 2.3-litre inline-four producing 150hp - a robust, simple engine that established the M Class as a premium SUV contender. In 2002, the ML 350 joined the range with the M112 3.7-litre V6, delivering 235hp and representing a significant step up in refinement and power. These petrol variants offered a refined alternative to the diesel CDI models for owners prioritising smooth power delivery.

milestones.description: 2001 - ML 230 continues as entry-level petrol option
End of W163 production; ML 230 and ML 350 replaced by W164 generation with M272 V6

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz M Class 230 and 350 petrol is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points - from M111 timing chain wear to M112 harmonic balancer separation.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz M Class 230/350 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The M Class 230's M111 inline-four and the 350's M112 V6 are among Mercedes' most straightforward petrol engines - simple, robust, and capable of 150,000+ miles with proper maintenance. However, both have well-documented weak points that become more pronounced with age and mileage. The M111 suffers from timing chain wear and harmonic balancer issues, while the M112 is prone to harmonic balancer rubber separation and oil leaks. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
